title: Analysis of autophagy deficiency and cytotoxicity in autophagy-deficient human embryonic stem cell-derived neurons
protocol: Warm the pre-prepared NP culture medium without growth factors at 37°C in a water bath for at least 30 min.
Make up 40 mL of complete NP culture medium by adding 8 μL EGF and 8 μL FGF-2 to the pre-prepared NP culture medium.
Mix the complete NP culture medium by inversion.
Remove laminin solution from plates.
Add NP culture medium (1 ml per well) to the wells.
Warm the plates in the incubator at 37°C.
Remove frozen NP vials from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thaw at 37°C in a water bath.
Clean cryovial with ethanol.
Immediately transfer cells by adding dropwise to a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 8 mL of NP culture medium.
Spin cell suspension in a centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Remove supernatant completely, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of NP culture medium.
Take the PO-L coated warmed plate containing NP medium out of the incubator and add 1 mL cell suspension dropwise per well of 6-well plate.
Move plate gently in crisscross motion to distribute cells evenly in the well.
Place the plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C and do not disturb for at 48 h to allow the cells to attach.
Repeat the process for each cell line.
Culture hESC-derived NPs in a humidified incubator with 10% CO2 at 37°C.
Change media every day.
Aspirate media from NPs using a P1000 or vacuum pump system when culturing.
Passage cells once they become 100% confluent.
Split NPs at a 1:2 or 1:3 ratio, maintaining high density to promote cell growth and reduce differentiation risk.
Coat 6-well plates according to the first preparation step at least 24 hours before passaging cells.
Warm NP culture medium and DPBS at 37°C in a water bath for at least 10 minutes.
Remove laminin solution from PO-L coated plate, add NP culture medium (1 mL per well of 6-well plate), and warm the plate in an incubator at 37°C.
Remove media from 6-well plate containing NPs and wash cells once with DPBS.
Add Accutase dissociation reagent (1 mL per well of 6-well plate) dropwise to cover surface of well.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 3-5 minutes.
Gently tap the plate afterwards to dissociate cells.
Neutralize Accutase with 3 mL DPBS (1:3 ratio) per well.
Transfer cell suspension into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Tilt the plate and gently flush any remaining cells from the well with DPBS, collecting in Falcon tube.
Spin cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Remove supernatant completely without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL NP culture medium.
Take media-containing pre-warmed PO-L coated plate out of the incubator.
Add 1 mL cell suspension dropwise per well.
Move plate in a crisscross motion to distribute cells evenly.
Place plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C and do not disturb for 24 h to allow the cells to attach.
Warm NP culture medium, DPBS, and KnockOut Serum Replacement (KOSR) at 37°C in a water bath for at least 10 min.
Remove laminin solution from PO-L coated flask.
Add 14 mL NP culture medium and warm the flask in incubator at 37°C.
Remove media from T75 flask containing the NPs.
Wash cells once with DPBS.
Remove DPBS and add 2 mL of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA to dissociate the cells.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 1–3 min.
Gently tap the flask afterwards.
Quench Trypsin-EDTA with 1 mL KOSR.
Dilute the mixture further with 7 mL NP culture medium and transfer into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Spin cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 min at 21°C.
Remove supernatant completely without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL NP culture medium.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension to a PO-L coated flask containing warmed NP medium.
Move the flask in a crisscross motion to distribute cells evenly.
Place the flask in a humidified incubator at 37°C for 24 hours.
Prepare NP freezing medium (1 mL per cryovial) and keep it at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of NP freezing medium and transfer into a labelled cryovial.
Place the cryovial into a freezing chamber at -80°C freezer before transferring to liquid nitrogen after 24 hours.
Seed hESC-derived NPs at appropriate densities for neuronal differentiation.
Culture hESC-derived NPs in the presence of bFGF and EGF to commit them to forebrain fates.
Withdraw growth factors to terminally differentiate hESC-derived NPs into human neurons.
Maintain neuronal cultures up to 4-5 weeks if necessary, but experiments can be conducted on 3-weeks old neurons.
Differentiate hESC-derived NPs into neurons.
Dissociate the NPs in 6-well plate according to steps 2biv–x (or steps 2civ–xi if using flasks) and seed NPs into appropriate PO-L coated plates for experiments.
Switch from NP culture medium to neuronal differentiation medium containing N-2 and B-27 supplements without EGF and FGF-2.
Warm neuronal differentiation medium at 37°C in a water bath for at least 30 min.
Remove laminin solution from PO-L coated plate, add neuronal culture medium (1 ml, 500 μl or 100 μl per well of 6-, 24- or 96-well plate, respectively) and warm the plate in incubator at 37°C.
Resuspend NP cell pellet in 1 ml neuronal differentiation medium from steps 2bx or 2cix.
Count cells using 10 μL cell suspension and Trypan Blue staining.
Adjust cell suspension volume with neuronal differentiation medium according to Table 1.
Add 1 mL, 500 μL, or 100 μL of adjusted cell suspension per well of a 6-well, 24-well, or 96-well plate, respectively.
Seed one 6-well plate per NP line for immunoblotting analysis.
Seed a 24-well plate containing glass coverslips with at least three replicates of each cell line for immunofluorescence and TUNEL staining.
Seed a 96-well plate containing at least six replicates of each cell line for the cytotoxicity assay.
Place plates in a humidified incubator at 37°C without disturbance for 24 hours to allow cells to attach.
Culture cells in neuronal differentiation medium for 3-4 weeks.
Change medium every alternate day using a P1000 pipette or multichannel pipette, as appropriate.
Tilt the plate and remove 70% of the media from each well slowly to avoid disrupting neurons.
Replenish with fresh, pre-warmed neuronal differentiation medium gently.
Seed hESC-derived NPs into 6-well plates for immunoblotting analysis.
Differentiate hESC-derived NPs for 3–4 weeks into neurons according to step 3.
Harvest hESC-derived NPs upon confluency or differentiated neurons after 3-4 weeks for immunoblotting.
Prepare lysate for immunoblotting analysis of ATG5, LC3B, p62 and GAPDH in hESC-derived NPs and neurons.
Remove medium from cells and wash each well gently with 1 mL DPBS, then remove slowly.
Harvest cells using 1 mL DPBS per well, scraping to detach cells using a cell scraper.
Pool 2 wells into one Eppendorf tube for each cell line, creating n = 3 from one 6-well plate.
Keep harvested cell suspension on ice.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 2400 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and keep cell pellets on ice.
Resuspend cell pellets in an appropriate volume of Lysis Buffer with protease inhibitor cocktail, depending on pellet size.
Sonicate the cell lysates at 9 kHz for 10 seconds, repeat three times.
Vortex cell lysates for 5 seconds and incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 9600 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Collect supernatant (cell lysate) of each sample in a new Eppendorf tube and keep on ice.
Discard pellets (cell debris).
Quantify protein concentration in cell lysate using Bio-Rad Protein Assay Kit II according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Prepare to load 20 μg protein per cell lysate.
Adjust loading volume of cell lysate by making up to 10–20 μL using Lysis Buffer containing protease inhibitor cocktail.
Add 2–4 μL of 6× SDS loading dye to the adjusted sample volume.
Vortex the cell lysate and dye mixture for 5 s.
Boil samples at 95°C for 5 min on a heating block.
Load appropriate volume of the cell lysate dye mixture containing 20 μg of protein into a 12% precast polyacrylamide gel, such as 12–24 μL per sample and 10 μL of a protein ladder.
Perform SDS-PAGE using 1× Running Buffer under 120 V for 2–2.5 h until the smallest molecular weight marker reaches the bottom of the gel (∼10 kDa).
Transfer the protein from polyacrylamide gel onto methanol-activated PVDF membrane under 90 V for 90 min on ice using 1× Transfer Buffer with methanol.
Block PVDF membrane in 5% skimmed milk in PBS-T for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate each membrane with respective primary antibodies for ATG5, LC3B, and GAPDH on a rocking platform overnight at 4°C.
Wash membranes 6 times with PBS-T for 10 minutes each time on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Incubate each membrane with appropriate HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies on a rocking platform for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash membranes 6 times with PBS-T for 10 minutes each time on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Add ECL Western Blotting Detection Reagent to each membrane for 1 minute at room temperature, followed by exposing and developing on autoradiography film to visualize signal.
Strip the top part of the membrane with Stripping Buffer at 65°C for 15 minutes.
Block the membrane as in step 5d.
Incubate the membrane with primary antibody for p62 on a rocking platform overnight at 4°C.
Seed hESC-derived NPs into 96-well PO-L coated plates.
Differentiate hESC-derived NPs into neurons according to step 3.
Measure cytotoxicity after 3 weeks of neuronal differentiation using CytoTox-Glo Cytotoxicity Assay.
Perform CytoTox-Glo Cytotoxicity Assay on hESC-derived neurons according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure basal cytotoxicity from dead cells in the population (first reading).
Prepare AAF-Glo Assay Reagent from 5 mL Assay Buffer and AAF-Glo Substrate powder.
Gently remove old media.
Slowly add 100 μL fresh neuronal differentiation medium to each well of a 96-well plate.
Avoid harsh pipetting as this will detach the neuronal network from the bottom of the well.
Gently add 50 μL AAF-Glo solution to each well of the 96-well plate.
Slowly pipette up and down twice to mix.
Cover the plate with foil.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Measure luminescence with a microplate reader, taking two readings to average.
Prepare Lysis Reagent from 5 mL Assay Buffer and 33 μL Digitonin according to Promega Kit instructions.
Gently add 50 μL of the prepared Lysis Reagent to each well of a 96-well plate.
Slowly pipette up and down twice to mix the contents in each well thoroughly.
Cover the plate with foil.
Incubate the plate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Measure luminescence with a microplate reader 15 minutes after lysis.
Measure luminescence again with a microplate reader at 30 minutes after lysis, keeping the plate covered in foil.
Measure luminescence one final time with a microplate reader at 60 minutes after lysis, ensuring the plate remains covered in foil between measurements.
Determine basal cytotoxicity normalized to the total cell population.
Normalize the cytotoxicity data by dividing the first reading (basal cytotoxicity per well) with the second reading (indicative of total cell population per well).
Express the data as a percentage.
Perform TUNEL assay using Click-iT Plus TUNEL Assay for In Situ Apoptosis Detection, Alexa Fluor 488 dye (Invitrogen) on hESC-derived neurons, according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Make up solutions from kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Remove media from each well of 24-well plate.
Wash once with 200 μL DPBS without shaking.
Fix cells on each coverslip with 200 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde for 15 min at room temperature.
Slowly remove PFA.
Permeabilize cells with 200 μL of 0.25% Triton X-100 in DPBS per well.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature without shaking.
Wash each coverslip slowly and gently twice with 200 μL deionized water per well for 5 min at room temperature.
Incubate each coverslip with 100 μL of TdT Reaction Buffer per well for 10 min at 37°C in a humidified incubator.
Make up TdT reaction mixture according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Remove TdT Reaction Buffer slowly.
Gently add 50 μL TdT reaction mixture to each coverslip per well.
Incubate in a humidified incubator for 60 min at 37°C.
Wash each coverslip slowly and gently twice with 200 μL of 3% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) in DPBS per well for 5 min at room temperature without shaking.
Make up fresh TUNEL Reaction Buffer Additive according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Use the prepared buffer to make up TUNEL reaction cocktail according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Immediately add 50 μL of TUNEL reaction cocktail to each coverslip per well slowly and carefully.
Cover the plate in foil and incubate in a humidified incubator for 30 min at 37°C.
Gently remove the reaction cocktail from each well.
Wash each coverslip slowly and gently twice with 200 μL of 3% BSA in DPBS per well for 5 min at room temperature without shaking.
Block each coverslip with 300 μL of 3% BSA in DPBS per well for 1 h at room temperature on a flat surface without shaking while covering the plate in foil.
Add 200 μL of TUJ1 antibody diluted in 3% BSA in DPBS (1:200) to each coverslip per well.
Incubate overnight at 4°C on a flat surface without shaking.
Wash each coverslip slowly and gently twice with 200 μL of DPBS per well for 5 min at room temperature without shaking while covering the plate in foil.
Add 200 μL of Alexa Fluor 594 secondary antibody diluted in 3% BSA in DPBS (1:1000) to each coverslip per well.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature on a flat surface without shaking.
Wash each coverslip slowly and gently twice with 200 μL of DPBS per well for 5 min at room temperature without shaking while covering the plate in foil.
Mount each coverslip onto a glass slide using ProLong Gold antifade reagent with DAPI.
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 15–30 min.
Seal coverslips onto glass slides using nail varnish, taking care not to move the coverslips on the surface of glass slides.
Assess the number of TUNEL+ apoptotic nuclei in TUJ1+ cells.
Analyze at least 200 TUJ1+ cells per sample.
Calculate the percentage of TUNEL+ apoptotic nuclei in the total number of TUJ1+ cells analyzed for each sample.
